key_insight: Multiwavelength photoluminescence non-destructively reveals depth-dependent UV damage, identifying preferential degradation at the buried hole-transport-layer interface in p-i-n perovskite solar cells.
engineering_relevance: The approach enables rapid interface-stability screening, while 3-mercaptopropyltrimethoxysilane modification reduces buried-interface damage and improves UV stability.
method: Use wavelength-dependent absorption to probe degradation at different depths.
Combine wide-field PL imaging, time-resolved PL, and ideality-factor measurements under UV light-soaking.
Compare perovskite films and photovoltaic devices with different ITO surface modifiers.
evidence_signal: Nondestructive measurements localized UV degradation near the HTL interface, consistent with ex-situ destructive tests, and showed improved UV stability with silane modification.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative stability gains or validation under broader operational stressors; the reported method is optical characterization, not AI.
paper_title: Multiwavelength Photoluminescence as a Non-destructive Probe of Depth-Dependent UV Damage in Perovskite Semiconductors
